news.text: 5 February saw **André the Giant** controversially defeat **Hulk Hogan** for the WWF World Heavyweight Championship on NBC's *The Main Event*. Unknown to Hogan, Ted DiBiase had bribed twin referee Earl Hebner to take his brother Dave's place and deliver a bogus three-count while Hogan's shoulder remained off the canvas. André immediately surrendered the championship belt to DiBiase, prompting WWF president Jack Tunney to declare the title vacant and set up an undisputed tournament at *WrestleMania IV*.
news.youtube: Hulk Hogan vs Andre the Giant The Main Event 1988

news.text: 5 February saw the inaugural **Red Nose Day** telethon broadcast live on BBC One by charity **Comic Relief**. Fronted by comedian Lenny Henry and featuring sketches from the casts of *Blackadder* and *The Young Ones*, the evening introduced red foam noses across British high streets and raised over £15 million for causes in the UK and Africa. The runaway success demonstrated that the British public was remarkably willing to look completely ridiculous if the proceeds went to a worthy cause.
news.youtube: Comic Relief Red Nose Day 1988 first telethon

news.text: 9 February saw MPs vote 318 to 264 to allow television cameras into the **House of Commons** on an experimental basis. Prime Minister **Margaret Thatcher** opposed the reform out of concern for the chamber's dignity, but cross-party support secured an experiment that would finally bring Parliamentary debate into living rooms. Critics warned of shameless political grandstanding for the lenses, though observers noted that MPs were already remarkably adept at doing so untelevised.

10 February saw the Japanese launch of the role-playing game *Dragon Quest III* on the **Family Computer**, sparking widespread public commotion. Over one million copies were snapped up on day one as thousands of school pupils and workers played truant to queue around city blocks. The sheer level of disruption and retail chaos prompted publisher **Enix** to pledge that future instalments would only ever be released on weekends.
news.youtube: Dragon Quest III Famicom 1988 launch queues

news.text: 14 February saw British plasterer **Eddie the Eagle** Edwards leap into sporting folklore at the **Winter Olympics** in Calgary. Competing in the normal hill ski jump while wearing thick glasses that constantly fogged up, he finished comfortably in last place but won over spectators worldwide through sheer unvarnished pluck. His cheerful refusal to be embarrassed by elite competition prompted Olympic officials to swiftly rewrite entry rules to prevent such delightful amateurism happening again.
news.youtube: Eddie the Eagle Calgary 1988 ski jump

news.text: 14 February saw Australian soap star **Kylie Minogue** climb to number one on the UK singles chart with her debut release *I Should Be So Lucky*. Crafted by the hitmaking trio **Stock Aitken Waterman**, the unashamedly bubbly pop track spent five weeks at the summit and turned the *Neighbours* actress into a fixture of British chart history. Snobbish music critics predicted her career would last until roughly Easter, underestimating both her determination and her audience.
news.youtube: Kylie Minogue I Should Be So Lucky official video 1988

news.text: 15 February saw the premiere of science fiction sitcom *Red Dwarf* on **BBC Two**. Created by Rob Grant and Doug Naylor, the debut episode introduced **Craig Charles** as slovenly technician Dave Lister, who awakens from three million years in suspended animation to find himself the last surviving human in the cosmos. His only companions aboard the lonely mining ship are a conceited hologram, a vain humanoid descended from his pet cat, and a senile ship's computer.
news.youtube: Red Dwarf The End first episode 1988

news.text: 15 February saw the death of theoretical physicist and Nobel laureate **Richard Feynman** at the age of 69 in Los Angeles. Celebrated for his work in **quantum electrodynamics** and his colourful memoirs, Feynman had also famously unpicked the mechanical failures of the Space Shuttle Challenger disaster using a glass of iced water. His reported parting words wryly noted that dying was boring, having had quite enough of doing it once.
